help.general:
wgal: WG Always Live from the command line.

Usage: wgal [--json] [--lang <tag>] <command> [arguments]

State:
  status                     the watchdog and every tunnel
  list                       the registered tunnels
  show <tunnel>              one tunnel in full
  discover                   the tunnels WGAL can watch, registered or not
  log [...]                  the event log

Tunnels:
  register <tunnel>          start watching a tunnel
  unregister <tunnel> --yes  forget it (the tunnel itself is not touched)
  monitor <tunnel> on|off    probe it, or not
  set <tunnel> [...]         probe timing and targets
  auto-recovery <tunnel> on|off
  start-when-stopped <tunnel> on|off
  retry <tunnel> [...]       how often to try recovering again
  connect|reconnect <tunnel>, disconnect <tunnel> --yes
  probe <tunnel>             probe its targets now
  pause, resume              monitoring of every tunnel

Notifications:
  notify [...]               Telegram settings, Bot Token, a test, the language
  language [<tag>|--clear]   the language of wgal and of the Telegram messages

Other:
  host [...]                 worker threads and time zone
  mcp on|off, mcp telegram on|off
  export, import [...]       the settings file, on standard output and input
  help [command], --version

<tunnel> is the tunnel's WGAL ID, as "wgal list" and "wgal discover" show it.
--json writes one JSON object to standard output instead of text.
--lang <tag> writes this one command in another language ("wgal language").
Exit codes: 0 done; 1 refused, or done with a failed result; 2 a mistake in
the arguments or the input (nothing changed); 3 the watchdog could not be
reached (nothing changed); 4 it may have been carried out, but that is not
confirmed.
help.topic.auto_recovery:
wgal auto-recovery <tunnel> on|off
  Lets WGAL restart the tunnel when traffic stops. It turns on only once the
  recovery target has answered a probe through the tunnel.
help.topic.connect:
wgal connect <tunnel> [--wait S | --no-wait]
  Starts the tunnel and waits until it settles (30 s, at most 120).
  Exit 1 when it did not connect, or no traffic gets through it while it is
  monitored.
help.topic.disconnect:
wgal disconnect <tunnel> --yes [--wait S | --no-wait]
  Stops the tunnel: whatever goes through it stops too, a remote session
  included.
help.topic.discover:
wgal discover
  The tunnels the official WireGuard manager has that WGAL can watch, and
  which are registered.
help.topic.export:
wgal export > wgal-settings.json
  Writes the settings file (no device name, chat ID or Bot Token) to standard
  output.
help.topic.host:
wgal host [--workers N|auto] [--time-zone NAME|system]
  Worker threads (2-17, or auto for the suggested count) and the time zone
  messages and the log use (an IANA name such as Asia/Taipei, or system).
help.topic.import:
wgal import [--match name|id] [--register-missing] [--monitor-new]
            (--dry-run | --yes) < wgal-settings.json
  Reads a settings file from standard input (at most 64 KiB) and applies it.
  --dry-run shows what would change. Exit 1 when any part failed, an automatic
  recovery that was refused included; the parts done are not undone.
help.topic.language:
wgal language                the language wgal writes in, the messages',
                             and the 13 to choose from
wgal language <tag>          wgal writes in it from now on, and so do the
                             Telegram messages
wgal language --clear        back to English for wgal (the messages keep
                             theirs); do this before going back to a
                             version before 4.0.0
wgal --lang <tag> <command>  one command in another language (--lang en)
  Commands, options and values (on, off, --yes) are the same in every
  language.
help.topic.list:
wgal list
  The registered tunnels, one line each.
help.topic.log:
wgal log [--tunnel <tunnel> | --system | --watchdog] [--before SEQ]
  One page of the event log, newest first; "More: wgal log --before N" gives
  the next.
help.topic.mcp:
wgal mcp on|off
wgal mcp telegram on|off
  Lets agents use WGAL through wgal-mcp, and lets them set Telegram. Turning
  either on asks you to type yes, in an interactive terminal only. This only
  keeps an agent from turning them on in passing: anything run as this account,
  an agent with a shell too, can use wgal as you.
help.topic.monitor:
wgal monitor <tunnel> on|off
  Probes the tunnel and acts on what it finds, or not.
help.topic.notify:
wgal notify                        the notification settings
wgal notify on|off                 notifications for this computer
wgal notify device <name>          the device name messages give
wgal notify chat <id> | --clear    the Telegram chat ID
wgal notify tunnel <tunnel> on|off one tunnel's notifications
wgal notify token set              asks for the Bot Token unseen (or reads
                                   one line of standard input when it is
                                   not a terminal)
wgal notify token clear --yes      removes the Bot Token
wgal notify test [--wait S]        sends a test message and waits for Telegram
wgal notify language [<tag>]       lists the languages, or writes the
                                   messages in one (only the messages;
                                   "wgal language <tag>" sets wgal's too)
  The Bot Token is never taken from the command line or the environment.
  Should the terminal stop showing what you type (wgal was killed while it
  asked for the token), "stty echo" brings it back on Linux and macOS.
help.topic.pause:
wgal pause
  Pauses monitoring of every tunnel: no probes and no automatic actions until
  "wgal resume".
help.topic.probe:
wgal probe <tunnel> [--wait S | --no-wait]
  Probes its targets now and shows what each answered; exit 1 when one did not.
  While monitoring is off it is a one-off check that changes nothing else.
help.topic.reconnect:
wgal reconnect <tunnel> [--wait S | --no-wait]
  Stops and starts the tunnel, and waits until it settles.
help.topic.register:
wgal register <tunnel>
  Starts watching the tunnel (an ID from "wgal discover"). Then give it a
  recovery target with "wgal set".
help.topic.resume:
wgal resume
  Resumes monitoring of every tunnel that has it on.
help.topic.retry:
wgal retry <tunnel> [--limit N|forever] [--interval S]
  After the first recovery round fails: up to N more rounds (0-3600) or forever,
  one every S seconds (10-10800). What is not given stays.
help.topic.set:
wgal set <tunnel> [--interval S] [--timeout S] [--retries N] [--min-fault S]
                   [--recovery-target T|none] [--observe T]... [--no-observe]
  Changes only what is given. --interval 10-3600 s between probes;
  --timeout 1-10 s;
  --retries 0-10 failed rounds before a fault; --min-fault 0-3600 s.
  T is an IPv4 address (ICMP) or address:port (a TCP connect), reachable only
  through the tunnel. --observe may be given up to 8 times and replaces the
  list.
  If someone else changes the same settings meanwhile, the later change wins.
help.topic.show:
wgal show <tunnel>
  One tunnel in full: its light, targets and their last probes, timing,
  retries, switches and incident.
help.topic.start_when_stopped:
wgal start-when-stopped <tunnel> on|off
  Lets WGAL start the tunnel again when something other than WGAL stopped it.
help.topic.status:
wgal status
  The watchdog's version, the monitoring pause, MCP, notifications and every
  tunnel, one line each.
help.topic.unregister:
wgal unregister <tunnel> --yes
  Makes WGAL forget the tunnel and its settings. The tunnel itself, and
  whether it starts at boot, are not touched.
hint.baseline_not_passed: The recovery target has not answered a probe through the tunnel yet: set a target reachable only through it ("wgal set"), probe it ("wgal probe"), then try again
hint.binding_lost: The official WireGuard manager no longer has this tunnel; register it again once it does
hint.busy: Wait a few seconds and try again
hint.caller_not_allowed: This account is not on this installation's access list
hint.cannot_control: The official WireGuard manager does not let WGAL start or stop this tunnel
hint.needs_administrator_or_listed_tunne: The tunnel is not on this installation's access list; only an administrator may do this
hint.operation_in_progress: WGAL is starting or stopping this tunnel now: wait a few seconds and try again
hint.secret_store_unavailable: The place WGAL keeps the Bot Token cannot be used right now; try again later
hint.storage_failed: WGAL cannot store its state right now, so this step changed nothing. Try again later
hint.tunnel_not_discovered: The official WireGuard manager does not list this tunnel: "wgal discover" lists the ones it has
hint.tunnel_not_registered: WGAL does not monitor this tunnel: "wgal discover" lists the ones it can, "wgal register" adds one
hint.unknown_time_zone: Use an IANA time zone name such as Asia/Taipei, Europe/Berlin or UTC
input.answer_unreadable: the answer could not be read ({error})
input.import_too_large: the settings file on standard input is larger than {kib} KiB; nothing was changed
input.no_token: no Bot Token was given; nothing was changed

input.not_a_token: that is not a Telegram Bot Token; nothing was changed
input.not_a_token_shape: that is not a Telegram Bot Token (3 to 15 digits, ':', then 30 to 40 letters, digits, '_' or '-'); nothing was changed
input.stdin_unreadable: standard input could not be read ({error}); nothing was changed
input.token_line_too_long: the line is longer than {bytes} bytes, far longer than a Bot Token; nothing was changed
input.token_unreadable: the Bot Token could not be read ({error}); nothing was changed
language.built_in_chinese: Traditional Chinese (the built-in texts of a watchdog older than 3.0.0)
language.list_heading: Languages ("wgal language <tag>" picks one for wgal and the Telegram messages, "wgal --lang <tag> <command>" for one command):
language.other_texts: {language} ({tag}), in texts other than this wgal's (another version handed them over)
language.shared_unknown: {tag}, which this wgal does not have, so it writes in English
language.unknown: a set this wgal does not know ({id})
notify.language_unknown: {tag} is not one of the languages: {tags}; nothing was changed

show.auto_recovery_pending: {state} (turns on once the recovery target passes its baseline check)

show.monitoring_running: Monitoring: running; storage: {storage}; worker threads: {running} running of {workers}

unwritten.changed: the result could not be written to standard output ({error}); the change itself was carried out: run "wgal status" to see
unwritten.failed: the result could not be written to standard output ({error}); the failure and what was done before it are said above
unwritten.read: the result could not be written to standard output ({error}); nothing was changed
usage.confirm_disconnect: this stops the tunnel: whatever goes through it stops too, a remote session included; add --yes to do it. Nothing was changed
usage.confirm_import: this changes the settings the file holds (try --dry-run first to see what would change); add --yes to do it. Nothing was changed
usage.confirm_token_clear: this removes the Bot Token: no Telegram message can be sent until one is set again; add --yes to do it. Nothing was changed
usage.confirm_unregister: this makes WGAL forget the tunnel and its settings (the tunnel itself is not touched); add --yes to do it. Nothing was changed
usage.give_device_name: give the device name (in quotes when it has spaces)
usage.give_tunnel: give the tunnel's WGAL ID ("wgal list" or "wgal discover" shows them)
usage.help_takes_one: "wgal help" takes at most one command
usage.import_needs_stdin: give the settings file on standard input, as in "wgal import --dry-run < wgal-settings.json"; nothing was changed
usage.lang_twice: --lang is given more than once; give one of: {tags}
usage.lang_unknown: {tag} is not one of the languages: {tags}
usage.language_or_clear: give a language or --clear, not both
usage.mcp_forms: give "wgal mcp on|off" or "wgal mcp telegram on|off"
usage.mcp_needs_terminal: turning this on is asked of a person: run it in an interactive terminal (standard input and output both a terminal). Nothing was changed
usage.not_a_chat_id: {argument} is not a Telegram chat ID: 1 to 19 digits not starting with 0 (a leading - for a group), or @username
usage.not_a_notify_command: {argument} is not a notify command: give on, off, device, chat, tunnel, token, test or language
usage.not_a_number: {option} must be a whole number from {min} to {max}, not {argument}
usage.not_a_time_zone: {argument}: {reason}; give an IANA name such as Asia/Taipei, Europe/Berlin or UTC, or system
usage.not_a_tunnel_id: {argument} is not a tunnel ID: 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, '-' or '_' ("wgal list" shows them)
usage.not_utf8: an argument is not valid UTF-8
usage.nothing_to_set: give at least one setting to change
usage.one_log_filter: give at most one of --tunnel, --system and --watchdog
usage.target_bad_port: {option} {argument} is not a target: the port is not 1 to 65535; give an IPv4 address such as 192.0.2.1 (ICMP) or address:port such as 192.0.2.1:443 (TCP)
usage.target_not_ipv4: {option} {argument} is not a target: not an IPv4 address; give an IPv4 address such as 192.0.2.1 (ICMP) or address:port such as 192.0.2.1:443 (TCP)
usage.target_refused: {option} {argument} is not a target: {reason}; give an IPv4 address such as 192.0.2.1 (ICMP) or address:port such as 192.0.2.1:443 (TCP)
usage.token_forms: give "wgal notify token set" (it asks for the token unseen) or "wgal notify token clear --yes"
usage.token_on_command_line: an argument is shaped like a Telegram Bot Token. A Bot Token is never taken from the command line, where it stays in the shell's history and other programs can see it; the token was not sent anywhere. If it is your real token, consider getting a new one from @BotFather, then set it with "wgal notify token set", which asks for it unseen
